chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The dower (mahr) is anything upon which the people agree, whether little or much, in a temporary marriage or a permanent marriage.

key_terms.الصَّدَاقُ: Dower or mahr, the gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What determines the amount of dower (mahr) in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this foundational narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the principle of 'taraadun' (mutual consent) as the sole determinant for the dower (sadaq), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the amount is a contractual right rather than a fixed statutory obligation. This definition underscores the flexibility of Islamic marriage contracts, allowing the dower to vary according to social norms and individual agreement in both temporary (mut'ah) and permanent (zawaj) unions. The hadith serves as a key legal basis for rejecting rigid traditionalism in favor of contextual mutual agreement.
